title: DINO: DETR with Improved DeNoising Anchor Boxes for End-to-End Object Detection
grouping: One wide light-grey rounded block 'Decoder Layers x M' spans the figure; the query inputs below it and outputs above it are grouped into two CDN groups, each split by brackets into three positive and three negative queries. To the right, a separate square inset shows how positive and negative boxes are made.
shapes_depth: Flat. Each query is a small two-part cell: a top half filled yellow (positive) or dark olive-brown (negative) over a peach bottom half; outputs repeat the same cells. Above them grey rounded label boxes name the target: 'reconstruction loss' over positives, 'no object' over negatives. The inset is a dark olive square ('negative') containing a yellow square ('positive') crossed by a horizontal line with tick marks lambda_1 and lambda_2 for the two noise scales. Thin black arrows; serif text.
proposed_highlight: The idea - positive vs negative denoising queries - is carried entirely by two fills (yellow, olive-brown) that are reused in the inset; the decoder itself is a plain grey slab.
lesson: Encode the two query kinds by one fill each and reuse exactly those fills in a small nested-square inset that shows the noise ranges, so the inset explains the main drawing's colour code.
notes: Venue ICLR from Semantic Scholar (venue_source: semantic-scholar); year = arXiv preprint year (2203.03605). elements 'other' = the nested-square noise inset.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

insights.structure: One wide grey 'Decoder Layers x M' slab spans the left of the figure, with a row of query cells below it and a matching row of output cells above it, both split into two 'CDN group' sets of three positive and three negative queries; a separate square inset sits to the right.
insights.data: Each query is a two-part cell (yellow or olive-brown top over a peach bottom); outputs reuse the same cells, and grey rounded label boxes above them name the target ('reconstruction loss' over positives, 'no object' over negatives).
insights.emphasis: The positive/negative idea is carried only by two fills, yellow and olive-brown, which the inset reuses as a yellow 'positive' square nested inside an olive 'negative' square, with lambda_1 and lambda_2 tick marks for the two noise radii.
insights.flow: Bottom to top: thin black arrows go up from each query into the slab and up again from each output to its label box; the inset has no arrows into the main drawing.
insights.avoid: The inset sits unlabelled and unconnected far to the right, so a reader must work out alone that it explains how the noise ranges make positive and negative boxes; the decoder is a featureless grey slab.

arrangement.units: one unframed composition: a grey slab between a row of input query cells and a row of output cells, grouped by brackets into two CDN groups; a separate square inset on the right
arrangement.inputs_as: rows of two-part query cells coloured by positive/negative, bracketed and labelled 'positive'/'negative' and 'CDN group0/1'
arrangement.losses_at: grey label boxes on top of each output group ('reconstruction loss', 'no object')
arrangement.shared: one decoder slab shared by both CDN groups
